---
title: "Glossary"
description: "What the numbers on Sparvi mean and how they're calculated."
---

## Pitching

**Stuff+**: Pitch quality graded only on physical traits (velocity, movement, spin, release point, extension, arm angle, and gaps from the pitcher's primary fastball). 100 is an average qualified MLB pitcher from the season before ({{< meta baseball.scale_ref_season >}}), and the scale stays fixed all season; 10 points is one standard deviation. Pitch-level grades are scaled within fastballs, breaking balls, and offspeed pitches. [How it's built](/baseball/stuff-plus/#method).

[**Location+**]{#location-plus}: Pitch quality graded only on where the pitch crossed the plate (side, mirrored so inside is the same for every batter, and height within the batter's rulebook zone), the count, and whether pitcher and batter are on the same side. Same target and same frozen scale as Stuff+. The zone comes from each batter's listed height ({{< meta baseball.loc_zone_bottom >}} to {{< meta baseball.loc_zone_top >}} of it), because Statcast's own zone fields changed definition in {{< meta baseball.season >}}. [How it's built](/baseball/stuff-or-command/#method).

**Pitching+**: Stuff+ inputs and Location+ inputs in one model, on the same scale.

**RV+**: Actual run value per 100 pitches, on the same scale as Stuff+.

**IVB (induced vertical break)**: How far a pitch finishes above or below where a spinless pitch would, in inches. High-IVB fastballs "ride"; curveballs have negative IVB.

**HB (horizontal break)**: Sideways movement in inches, **positive toward the pitcher's arm side** for both righties and lefties, so shapes compare directly.

**FB velo**: Average velocity of the pitcher's primary fastball: the four-seamer or sinker thrown most over the season. "Velo Δ14" compares that same pitch over the final 14 days with its season average.

[**Role (SP, RP, Swing)**]{#roles}: Set from how often a pitcher started, separately for each level and season. A **start** means he threw his team's first pitch of the game, so an opener gets the start and the pitcher who follows him doesn't. **SP**: at least {{< meta baseball.role_sp_min_share >}} of his games were starts, with at least {{< meta baseball.role_sp_min_starts >}} starts. **RP**: no more than {{< meta baseball.role_rp_max_share >}} of his games were starts. **Swing**: everyone in between, such as spot starters, pitchers who moved between the rotation and the bullpen, and MLB pitchers making a couple of rehab starts. Player pages show it as, for example, "SP · 27 G, 26 GS" (games, games started).

**Role-based pitch minimums**: The pitch-grade leaderboard and the Triple-A explorer hold each pitcher to his role's minimum by default. MLB: {{< meta baseball.q_mlb_sp >}}+ pitches for starters, {{< meta baseball.q_mlb_rp >}}+ for relievers and swingmen. Triple-A: {{< meta baseball.q_aaa_sp >}}+ and {{< meta baseball.q_aaa_rp >}}+. Typing a minimum overrides this for everyone.

**CSW rate**: Called strikes plus whiffs, divided by pitches.

[**Translated to MLB**]{#translation}: A Triple-A number run through its Triple-A → MLB line: the typical major-league value for players who posted that number in Triple-A before moving up (a weighted fit over the last two seasons' promotions). Each translation has a range that held {{< meta baseball.tr_band >}} of those players, and lines under {{< meta baseball.tr_min_aaa >}} PA or batters faced aren't translated. It describes where players like him have landed, not a forecast of his results. [How it's built](/baseball/aaa-translation/#method).

**Chase induced**: Share of pitches outside the zone that the hitter swung at.

## Hitting

**Chase rate**: Swings at pitches outside the strike zone ÷ pitches outside the zone. Bunt attempts are excluded.

**Zone swing / zone contact**: Swing rate on pitches in the zone, and contact rate on those swings.

**Whiff rate**: Swinging strikes ÷ swings. Foul tips count as whiffs, matching Baseball Savant.

**Hard-hit rate**: Share of balls in play hit 95+ mph.

**EV90**: The 90th-percentile exit velocity on balls in play. A steadier read on raw power than average or max exit velocity.

**xwOBA**: Expected weighted on-base average. Uses the expected value of each ball in play from exit velocity and launch angle, plus actual strikeouts, walks, and hit-by-pitches.

## Roster rules

[**Rule 5 eligible**]{#rule-5}: A player not on a 40-man roster whose protection window has run out can be taken by another club in the Rule 5 Draft. The window is five seasons for a player who was 18 or younger on the June 5 before his first pro contract, four for 19 or older. The [Rule 5 board](/baseball/tools/rule-5.html) estimates eligibility from signing dates and ages; its statuses are **Eligible** (signing date known), **Likely eligible** (signing date estimated from the draft year), and **Unknown** (no signing record). How well the estimate matched published lists is in the [method box](/baseball/rule-5/#method).

## Conventions

**Percentiles** rank a player against the qualified league pool and are **oriented so higher is always better**, so a low chase rate or a low walk rate allowed shows as a high percentile. Unqualified players are placed against the same qualified pool.

[**Org score**]{#org-score}: In [Which farm systems make players better?](/baseball/farm-systems/), an organization's average in-season change (second half of the Triple-A season minus first half, minus the league-wide change that season) across its qualifying Triple-A players, [shrunk](#shrinkage) toward the league average, with a 90% bootstrap interval and the number of players behind it. Positive always means improvement.

[**Shrinkage (empirical Bayes)**]{#shrinkage}: Pulling a noisy group average toward the overall average, by an amount set from the data. The spread between groups that exceeds what sampling noise alone would produce is estimated across all groups; each group's average then keeps only the share of its distance from the mean that's likely real. Small or noisy groups are pulled in more. When the groups differ no more than noise would, every score lands on the average.

[**Qualified pool**]{#qualified}: {{< meta baseball.min_pa_qualified >}}+ PA (hitters) or batters faced (pitchers) over a full season. Earlier in the season, and in the last-30-days window, the minimum is prorated to the share of the schedule played (team games so far ÷ a full season), with a floor of 25. At each level's final date this season, Triple-A teams had played a median of {{< meta baseball.aaa_final_team_games >}} of {{< meta baseball.aaa_full_season_games >}} games, so the Triple-A minimum is {{< meta baseball.aaa_final_qual >}}.

[**Snapshots and the date slider**]{#snapshots}: The leaderboard, Triple-A explorer, and player pages keep a weekly snapshot of every number: the last game on or before each Sunday, plus the final day. "Season to date" counts everything through that date; "last 30 days" only the 30 days before it. Roles and percentiles are as of each snapshot, and Stuff+ uses the same fixed scale throughout. The final season-to-date snapshot matches the season totals exactly.

**Δ14** compares the final (or most recent) 14 days with the season to date. Rates are in percentage points. [Why two weeks is enough for some numbers and not others](/baseball/two-week-signal/).

[**Strike zone**]{#strike-zone}: the rulebook zone, from {{< meta baseball.loc_zone_bottom >}} to {{< meta baseball.loc_zone_top >}} of the batter's listed height, as wide as the plate, and a pitch counts if any part of the ball touches it. It's the definition Statcast uses for MLB from {{< meta baseball.season >}} and for Triple-A throughout; earlier MLB seasons recorded a taller zone set from each batter's stance, so Sparvi applies the height-based zone to every season and level to keep chase and zone rates comparable.

## NFL {#nfl}

[**EPA per play**]{#nfl-epa}: Expected points added. Every snap starts with an expected number of points for the offense, given down, distance, field position, and time; EPA is how much the play changed it. A 6-yard gain on 3rd-and-5 adds more than on 3rd-and-10. Sparvi uses nflverse's EPA model. Defense numbers are EPA allowed, so lower is better.

[**Plays counted**]{#nfl-plays}: Passes (including sacks and scrambles) and runs with an EPA. Two-point tries, kneel-downs, and spikes are left out. Regular season only.

[**Success rate (NFL)**]{#nfl-success}: Share of plays with positive EPA (the nflverse convention). College football pages use a different, yards-based definition, noted where it applies.

**Pass/run splits**: Passes are dropbacks (attempts, sacks, and scrambles); runs are designed runs.

[**Early-down pass rate**]{#nfl-edpr}: Pass rate on 1st and 2nd down when the offense's win probability is between {{< meta nfl.neutral_wp_lo >}} and {{< meta nfl.neutral_wp_hi >}}, so blowouts and comebacks don't skew it.

[**PROE**]{#nfl-proe}: Pass rate over expected: actual pass rate minus nflverse's expected pass rate for the same situations (down, distance, field position, score, time), in percentage points. It describes tendency, not quality.

[**Explosive plays**]{#nfl-explosive}: Passes of {{< meta nfl.explosive_pass_yds >}}+ yards and runs of {{< meta nfl.explosive_run_yds >}}+, as a share of plays.

**Turnover rate**: Interceptions plus lost fumbles, per play.

[**Garbage time**]{#nfl-garbage}: 4th-quarter plays when the offense's win probability is below {{< meta nfl.garbage_wp_lo >}} or above {{< meta nfl.garbage_wp_hi >}}. Teams play differently with the game decided, so the default view removes these plays; every team view can include them.

[**Opponent-adjusted**]{#nfl-adjusted}: A team's own EPA/play with the strength of its opponents removed. Every play's EPA is fit on the offense, the defense, and home field together (ridge regression, as of each week), and each team is corrected by the average strength of the defenses (or offenses) it faced. The strength estimates use a penalty (λ = {{< meta nfl.adj_lambda >}} plays) chosen by how well they predict the next week's game margins. NFL schedules are balanced enough that the correction is usually small. [Details](/nfl/tools/team-efficiency.html).

**Season to date / last {{< meta nfl.trailing_weeks >}} weeks**: The week slider shows every number as of the end of each week. "Season to date" counts weeks 1 through that week; the trailing window only the last {{< meta nfl.trailing_weeks >}} weeks. The final week's season-to-date numbers match the season totals exactly.
